title: Multiheme Cytochrome c7 Expansion Is a Phylum-Level Trait of the Candidate Phylum Kryptonia: A Survey of 22,307 Prokaryotic Genomes
content: Background: Multiheme c-type cytochromes (MHCs) are the principal conduits of extracellular electron transfer (EET) in dissimilatory metal-reducing bacteria, yet their distribution across recently described candidate phyla remains poorly resolved. The cytochrome c7 family (triheme per core module) is a widespread MHC lineage whose phylum-level copy-number architecture has never been systematically surveyed. Methods: We scanned 22,307 prokaryotic genomes spanning candidate and established phyla with a dedicated c7-family profile HMM (E < 0.01), quantified per-genome copy numbers and CXXCH heme-binding motif loads, and benchmarked Kryptonia against Aquificota, DPANN, CPR, and a broad genomic background. Results: All 51 Kryptonia genomes encode c7 homologs, with a median of 15 copies per genome (max 19; 100% of genomes ≥5 copies; 88% ≥10) — the highest median per-genome dosage of any surveyed clade. By contrast, the largest Aquificota family (Aquificaceae) encodes a median of 1 copy, DPANN a median of 0 (max 6), and 98.9% of 20,217 background genomes carry fewer than 5. Kryptonia c7 proteins are also enriched in large MHCs: 49% carry ≥9 CXXCH motifs, versus 15–25% in CPR/DPANN. Canonical and divergent (novel) copies co-occur in 49/51 genomes, indicating a mixed repertoire rather than fixation of a single variant. Conclusions: High-copy, mixed-composition c7 repertoires are a phylum-level trait of Kryptonia rather than an isolate-specific anomaly, positioning this candidate phylum as a previously unrecognized reservoir of multiheme electron-transfer architecture.
